author: tom
title: Activity statements: the monthly number worth reading
dek: Every licensed bookmaker sends a statement of your wins, losses and deposits. Here is what to look for.
body:
Every licensed wagering provider in Australia sends account holders a regular activity statement. It is one of the most useful documents a punter receives, and one of the least read. A few minutes with it each month tells you more about your betting than any app screen.

What the statement shows

Statements are part of the National Consumer Protection Framework for online wagering. Your provider must make them available at least monthly, and you can usually download older ones from your account.

  • Deposits: every amount you added to the account, with dates and methods.
  • Withdrawals: what you took out, and when it was paid.
  • Bets placed: the number of bets and the total amount staked.
  • Net result: wins minus losses for the period, the single number that matters most.

What to look for

Start with the net result. It is the real cost of betting for the month, after the winning weekends and the losing ones have balanced out. Many people are surprised by it, in both directions, because memory favours the big wins.

Then compare deposits with the plan you set yourself. If you decided on $200 a month and deposited $350, the statement shows it in black and white. Repeated small top-ups are a common pattern: each feels minor, but together they move the total well past a budget.

Finally, look at the number of bets. A sharp rise from one month to the next often means betting has shifted from a weekend pastime to something more frequent, such as live betting during every match.

Reading several months together

One statement is a snapshot; three or four side by side show a trend. A simple table on paper or in a spreadsheet is enough.

July$180−$9522
August$240−$16031
September$410−$29058

In this example the deposits more than doubled in three months and the number of bets almost tripled. Nothing on any single day looked unusual, but the trend is clear.

If the numbers worry you

You do not need to wait for a bad month to act. Every licensed provider must let you set a deposit limit, and lowering one takes effect straight away. You can also take a break from your account, or register with BetStop to exclude yourself from every licensed online and phone provider at once.

Free, confidential support is available any time from Gambling Help Online on 1800 858 858 or at gamblinghelponline.org.au.

The takeaway

Put a monthly reminder in your calendar for the day your statement arrives. Read the net result, compare deposits with your plan, and check the trend over the last three months. It takes five minutes and keeps betting a choice rather than a habit.
